Over the past two decades, Al Aman Fund has become a leading national model in supporting orphaned youth beyond the age of 18. Established as a royal initiative by Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah and officially registered as a non-profit organization in 2006, Al Aman is the first institution of its kind in Jordan dedicated to serving this critical and often overlooked demographic. It was founded in response to an urgent need when orphaned youth leave care homes. Upon reaching the age of 18 they lose access to institutional support and must navigate adult life independently, often without guidance, stability or a clear path forward. Without a family safety net, continuing education or building a secure and dignified life becomes a significant challenge. To bridge this gap, Al Aman has developed a comprehensive support system that enables orphaned youth to pursue higher education in universities, colleges, and vocational training centers. Beyond covering tuition fees, Al Aman provides essential living support, including a monthly allowance, safe housing, health insurance, psychosocial support, and personal development programs, empowering beneficiaries to move forward with confidence and independence. The name “Al Aman,” meaning “Safety” or “Security”, reflects our mission to provide stability and support. Al Aman empowers orphaned youth by equipping them with practical tools for a better future.

Over the years, Al Aman has evolved from a traditional charitable model into one focused on long-term, sustainable empowerment. Our approach centers on building strong partnerships where every donor becomes a true partner investing in the future of orphaned youth. Together, we create lasting impact. Al Aman operates under a clear governance framework. The General Assembly sets the long-term vision and priorities; the Board of Directors oversees planning, performance, and accountability; and the General Manager and executive team manage daily operations and program implementation. It remains committed to the highest standards of transparency and accountability, with policies in place to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure responsible stakeholder engagement.
Providing orphaned youth with a better future and helping them become fully independent.
Equipping Orphaned youth with the education and skills needed to become self-reliant and productive members of society.

Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans supports orphaned youth graduating from care homes across all governorates of Jordan, ensuring 100% coverage for eligible youth. The Fund also accepts applications from orphaned youth whose living and financial conditions prevent them from continuing their education.

Applicants are selected based on clear criteria and the Fund’s available resources. To expand its social impact, the Fund continues to build strong partnerships with institutions in both the public and private sectors.
Eligibility applies to graduates of care homes who meet the Fund’s conditions for support.

sections.text: Al Aman Fund provides full scholarships for orphaned youth after they leave care homes, empowering them to build independent and confident futures. These scholarships fully cover tuition fees at public and private universities, community colleges, as well as vocational training centers. The Fund’s support also extends to orphaned youth across all governorates of the Kingdom, ensuring equal access to higher education through full coverage of public university education, and enabling them to achieve their aspirations.

Al Aman provides essential living support for orphaned youth after they leave care homes, ensuring stability and a dignified life. This support includes a monthly allowance, safe housing, and health insurance, enabling them to live with dignity as they transition into independent lives.

Al Aman Fund delivers integrated programs to develop the skills of orphaned youth, enhancing their self-confidence and increasing their readiness to enter the job market. The Fund has also developed a comprehensive competency framework known as “SIDE,” which includes 75 core skills used to assess youth capabilities and guide them toward the most suitable training programs. This framework is built on four main pillars; Social, Interpersonal, Digital, and Economic skills, ensuring holistic empowerment and equipping them to secure sustainable employment opportunities.

Psychosocial support and mental well-being are fundamental pillars in empowering orphaned youth after they leave care homes. Through the Step Towards Safety Program, Al Aman Fund provides comprehensive psychosocial support services, including group support sessions, individual mental health assessments, and one-to-one counseling and therapy sessions delivered in cooperation with specialized partners in the field. These services aim to strengthen mental well-being, build resilience, and enhance self-confidence, enabling youth to face life’s challenges with confidence and independence.

This program aims to promote the inclusion and active participation of orphaned youth in social, educational, cultural, and community-based activities. Through this program, Al Aman Fund provides opportunities for youth to engage with their communities, participate in volunteering and awareness initiatives, build positive relationships, strengthen their sense of belonging, and develop essential life and social skills within a supportive and inclusive environment.

The Order of Al Istiqlal (Independence) of the First Degree, bestowed by His Majesty King Abdullah II Ibn Al Hussein upon Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, stands as a distinguished royal recognition of a two-decade journey dedicated to supporting and empowering orphaned youth in Jordan, guided by the vision and unwavering support of Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah. Twenty years ago, Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans was founded by Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah with a clear vision: that orphaned youth in Jordan should never face adulthood alone or without opportunity. Over the past two decades, that vision has translated into measurable impact.

This policy applies to all Fund employees and temporary staff, volunteers and interns, service providers and contractors and partner entities handling Fund-related data.

It also covers data collected through the Fund’s official website, fund-affiliated digital applications and platforms, paper and electronic donation forms and communication channels (email, phone, social media).

– Employee records (e.g., personnel files, salary details, contact information).

– Individuals have the right to access, correct, or object to the use of their personal data.
How Do We Use Your Data?
– We obtain written consent before collecting personal information or using images in reports or media.
– Data is used only for internal purposes or for sharing success stories while respecting privacy.
– We do not sell, transfer, or publish any data to third parties without official authorization.
Data may be shared in the following cases:
– With the individual’s explicit written consent.

– With authorized donation-processing partners who follow strict privacy standards.

Note: All external parties must sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) before handling any Fund-related data.
How Do We Protect Your Data?
– Digital data is stored on secure servers protected by passwords, firewalls, and encryption.
– Physical documents are kept in locked cabinets within secure offices.
– Access to data is granted based on job roles and necessity.
– Staff are regularly trained on data privacy and protection best practices.
– All employees and volunteers must sign a privacy policy compliance pledge upon joining.
What Happens if There’s a Violation?
We take violations seriously. In such cases, we may launch an immediate internal investigation, apply disciplinary actions against those responsible and report serious breaches to legal authorities

body.text: Aqaba Development Corporation (ADC) and Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans have signed a strategic partnership agreement to support the educational journey of orphaned youth from Aqaba Governorate. Under the agreement, ADC will cover the educational costs of 15 orphaned youth for four years, as part of joint efforts aimed at empowering youth, expanding access to education, and enabling them to build more stable and sustainable professional futures.

The agreement was signed in the presence of Khaled Allawi, Executive Director of Corporate Affairs at Aqaba Development Corporation, and Eng. Noor Homoud, The Fund Director. The partnership reflects both organizations’ commitment to investing in human capital and creating educational and professional pathways for orphaned youth that strengthen their ability to achieve independence and self-reliance.

Khaled Allawi, Executive Director of Corporate Affairs at Aqaba Development Corporation, said that the partnership stems from ADC’s responsibility toward the local community in Aqaba and its belief that meaningful development cannot be achieved without investing in people and empowering young people to access opportunities that enable them to build their futures.

He emphasized that education is one of the most important pillars of empowerment, given its essential role in developing human capital and strengthening young people’s ability to participate effectively in economic and social development. He noted that supporting 15 young men and women from Aqaba over four years reflects ADC’s commitment to initiatives that create sustainable impact, moving beyond short-term support to create meaningful opportunities for the future.

Allawi added that Aqaba Development Corporation is proud of its partnership with Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, reaffirming the company’s commitment to directing its initiatives and corporate social responsibility programs toward creating tangible and sustainable impact in the lives of Aqaba’s youth. He highlighted the importance of building effective partnerships that respond to the genuine priorities and needs of the local community.

For her part, Eng. Noor Al-Hammoud, General Manager of Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, highlighted the importance of the partnership with Aqaba Development Corporation, noting that the education of orphaned youth and investment in their future lie at the heart of the Fund’s mission. She added that such partnerships provide young people with meaningful and sustainable opportunities to continue their education, develop their potential, and actively contribute to their communities.

Al Homoud stated that the impact of the partnership is not measured solely by the number of beneficiaries, but also by the broader opportunities it creates for each orphaned youth supported to pursue their education and build a more independent future. She also commended ADC’s commitment to ensuring that youth from the governorate directly benefit from these initiatives, further strengthening the impact of sustainable development and extending its positive outcomes to the wider community and the Kingdom.

The agreement forms part of ADC’s ongoing commitment to corporate social responsibility, supporting education, youth empowerment, and human capital development. It also aligns with Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans’ efforts over the past twenty years to provide education and development opportunities for orphaned youth after the age of 18, enabling them to become more independent and self-reliant.

The agreement also builds on the existing cooperation between the two organizations, which included the provision of vocational training scholarships during 2025 and 2026 in fields aligned with labor market needs.

body.text: Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans and The Specialty Hospital have signed a strategic partnership agreement, under which the hospital will join the Fund’s “Empowerment Partners” network. The partnership reflects the important role of Jordan’s healthcare sector in advancing corporate social responsibility and investing in the future of orphaned youth.

The four-year agreement was signed by Dr. Fawzi Al-Hammouri, Chairman and General Manager of The Specialty Hospital, and Eng. Noor Homoud, Al Aman Fund Director, in the presence of representatives from both organizations.

The partnership reflects The Specialty Hospital’s commitment to supporting community development and its belief in education as one of the most important pathways to empowering young people, particularly orphaned youth, and enabling them to build more secure and stable futures.

Under the agreement, The Specialty Hospital will provide four educational scholarships supporting the full educational journey of orphaned youth benefiting from Al Aman Fund. The scholarships will cover a range of academic disciplines, including healthcare related fields, particularly Nursing, as well as Cybersecurity.

The partnership will also provide students with opportunities for practical training at The Specialty Hospital during their studies, helping them gain hands-on experience, strengthen their readiness for the labour market, and pursue career pathways that support their independence upon completing their education. Commenting on the partnership, Dr. Fawzi Al-Hammouri, Chairman and General Manager of The Specialty Hospital, said: “At The Specialty Hospital, we believe that our responsibility towards our community extends beyond the provision of healthcare. It also includes investing in people and creating opportunities that enable orphaned youth to build their futures and become self-reliant.

Dr. Al-Hammouri also emphasized the importance of extending the partnership to the hospital’s employees by providing them with the opportunity to contribute to the education and empowerment of additional orphaned youth through Al Aman Fund’s monthly employee deduction program “Hours of Education”. This approach aims to strengthen the concept of shared social responsibility and embed giving as part of the institution’s culture among its employees. Speaking about the partnership, Eng. Noor Homoud, The Fund Director, said: “We are proud to welcome The Specialty Hospital to Al Aman Fund’s Empowerment Partners network, not only for the educational opportunities this partnership will provide, but also for what it represents: a genuine belief that empowering orphaned youth is a shared responsibility. We see this partnership as an inspiring example of the role Jordan’s healthcare sector can play in corporate social responsibility, where giving evolves beyond direct support into a meaningful investment in our youth’s futures, opening new opportunities for education, employment and self-reliance.”

The partnership builds on The Specialty Hospital’s longstanding approach to CSR and its participation in initiatives that serve the local community. It also reflects the hospital’s belief in the importance of collaboration among national institutions to advance sustainable development, invest in education, build young people’s capacities, and create meaningful career opportunities.

Following more than twenty years of impact, Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans continues to build strategic partnerships that create sustainable educational and career opportunities for orphaned youth. Its partnership with The Specialty Hospital highlights how cross-sector collaboration can turn corporate social responsibility into meaningful pathways towards education, employment and self-reliance.

news.title: Jordan Kuwait Bank Extends Strategic Partnership with Al Aman Fund Through 2030 to Empower Orphaned Youth
news.excerpt: Jordan Kuwait Bank has renewed its strategic partnership with Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans for the period 2026–2030, reflecting its long-term commitment to supporting the education of orphaned youth and empower

body.text: Jordan Kuwait Bank has renewed its strategic partnership with Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans for the period 2026–2030, reflecting its long-term commitment to supporting the education of orphaned youth and empowering them to complete their university studies and build more stable and independent futures.

Under the agreement, the Bank will provide educational scholarships to a number of young beneficiaries of Al Aman Fund, in cooperation with Jordanian universities across various governorates of the Kingdom. The scholarships will cover university tuition costs in accordance with the Fund’s approved criteria and academic pathways.

The partnership aims to support orphaned youth who have graduated from care homes registered with the Ministry of Social Development, where they spent most or all of their childhood, as well as orphaned youth supported by Ministry-registered orphan-care associations who live with one parent or members of their extended family and face challenging financial circumstances.

Group Chief Executive Officer Haitham Al-Batikhi, said that renewing the partnership reflects the Bank’s commitment to building long-term community partnerships capable of creating sustainable impact. He emphasized that investing in the education of orphaned youth equips them with the tools they need to shape their futures, strengthen their self-reliance, and participate actively in professional and community life.

Al-Batikhi added that the partnership with Al Aman Fund goes beyond providing educational support, representing an investment in orphaned youth’s potential and future. He noted that the continuation of the partnership through 2030 will enable more sustainable support throughout their university journey and help them transition from care toward independence and the development of their professional paths.

Eng. Noor Homour, Al Aman Fund Director, said that renewing the partnership with Jordan Kuwait Bank through 2030 represents a strong model of strategic partnership that goes beyond direct support, representing a long-term investment in people and creating meaningful, lasting impact in the lives of orphaned youth. She emphasized that education is one of the most important pathways for empowering youth to move confidently toward independence and build their futures.

She added: “We value this long-standing partnership because it reflects our shared belief that empowering orphaned youth is not achieved through a single opportunity, but through a long-term commitment that accompanies them through pivotal stages of their lives. We believe that every orphaned youth given the opportunity to pursue their education represents untapped potential for society and a success story whose impact can extend beyond the individual to their family, community, and country.

The renewed partnership builds on Jordan Kuwait Bank’s continued approach to supporting education and initiatives that create sustainable social impact, while contributing to Al Aman Fund’s efforts to empower its beneficiaries and provide them with opportunities to complete their education and build their futures independently.

news.title: Al Aman Fund and HyperMax Jordan Extend Partnership to Continue Empowering Orphaned Youth Through Education for the Second Year to Support the Back to Education Campaign
news.excerpt: Amman, Jordan – 18 August 2026: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans and HyperMax, the grocery retail brand wholly owned and operated by Majid Al Futtaim in Jordan, have announced the renewal of their strategic partner

body.text: Amman, Jordan – 18 August 2026: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans and HyperMax, the grocery retail brand wholly owned and operated by Majid Al Futtaim in Jordan, have announced the renewal of their strategic partnership for the second consecutive year to support Al Aman Fund’s ‘Back to Education’ Campaign.

The campaign aims to provide higher education scholarships and holistic support to orphaned youth who have graduated from care homes at 18, as well as orphaned youth from across the Kingdom. In addition to covering academic tuition, the campaign provides monthly allowances, housing support, and specialised capacity-building programmes to equip students with the skills needed to build independent, self-reliant futures.

Building on the success of their first year together, the renewed collaboration highlights HyperMax’s long-term commitment to corporate social responsibility and to supporting Al Aman Fund’s mission of community development. Throughout the campaign, HyperMax customers can easily contribute at checkout across all branches in Jordan by adding 10 piasters or more to their total bill – turning their everyday grocery trips into opportunities to create real, lasting change.

Commenting on the partnership, Engineer Noor Homoud, Al Aman Fund Director, said: “We greatly value our partnership with HyperMax for the second consecutive year, united by a shared commitment to creating meaningful opportunities for orphaned youth. This collaboration reflects the power of strategic partnerships in turning shared values into lasting impact.” She added: “Supporting the education of orphaned youth goes far beyond covering tuition fees; it gives them the opportunity to build their future with confidence and continue their journey toward independence and self-reliance. Through campaigns such as this, community members become active partners in our mission, helping orphaned youth pursue their dreams, realise their ambitions, and build brighter, more independent futures.”

Jerome Akel, Vice President of Commercial and Marketing at Majid Al Futtaim Retail – HyperMax Jordan, added: “At Majid Al Futtaim, we are deeply committed to creating lasting, positive impact in the communities we serve. Following the success of our collaboration last year, we are proud to extend our partnership with Al Aman Fund to support the Back to Education Campaign once again. By enabling our HyperMax customers to contribute directly at checkout, we are transforming everyday transactions into concrete opportunities for change. Together with our customers, we are providing orphaned youth with access to higher education, while equipping them with the tools and stability they need to build independent, fulfilling futures.” Last year’s campaign demonstrated the impact of collective giving, with HyperMax customers helping to fund a full academic year for 10 students. The campaign also covered monthly living allowances and a full year of housing rental for two students, enabling them to pursue their studies with greater stability.

news.title: Al Aman Fund Launched the Annual Back to Education Campaign to Support Orphaned Youth for the 2026/2027 Academic Year
news.excerpt: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has launched its annual Back to Education Campaign to support orphaned youth during the 2026/2027 academic year. The campaign comes as the Fund prepares to welcome a new cohort of o

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has launched its annual Back to Education Campaign to support orphaned youth during the 2026/2027 academic year. The campaign comes as the Fund prepares to welcome a new cohort of orphaned youth graduating from care homes, alongside eligible orphaned youth from across the Kingdom. It aims to raise donations to cover education costs, living expenses, and capacity building programs, while helping them navigate one of the most critical transitional stages of their lives.

Upon reaching the age of 18, orphaned youth living in care homes are required to leave institutional care and begin an independent chapter of their lives. Although they carry ambitions and aspirations for the future, many face new responsibilities and challenges without the continued family support or guidance available to their peers.

Al Aman Fund was established 20 years ago to support these orphaned youth during this transition, enabling them to continue their education and build more secure and stable futures. This year’s campaign holds particular significance as it marks two decades since the establishment of Al Aman Fund. The campaign seeks to cover the education costs of a new cohort of orphaned youth from across Jordan who have been admitted to public universities through the Unified Admission process.

The campaign’s support extends beyond education. It also includes housing, monthly allowances and health insurance, in addition to mental-health and capacity building programs delivered through SIDE curriculum. These programs are designed to help orphans youth move into the next stage of their lives with greater confidence, stability and reassurance.
Commenting on the campaign launch, Eng. Noor Homoud, The Fund Director, said:

“Every year, we welcome a new cohort of orphaned youth joining Al Aman family as they begin a new chapter in their lives after leaving care homes. These orphaned youth have great dreams and ambitions, and what they need most is an opportunity and a reliable support system that enables them to continue their education and build their futures with confidence and dignity.

“Through this campaign, we seek to provide that support and pave a safer path towards a better future, with the contribution of every individual and institution that believes education is the foundation of a stable life and a promising future. Every contribution opens a new door of security for an orphaned youth and brings them one step closer to the future they deserve.”
Al Aman Fund invites individuals and institutions to support the campaign through Zakat and Sadaqah, helping orphaned youth continue their education and build a better future.

Donations can be made through CliQ using the alias Amanfund, by calling 06 566 4427, or through the Fund’s website at: https://alamanfund.jo/ar/donate-ar Donations can also be made through eFAWATEERcom, electronic wallets and mobile applications, or by visiting Al-Aman Fund’s booth at City Mall, P1 level.

news.title: Strategic Partnership Between Al Aman Fund and Nova Services to Create Employment Opportunities for Al Aman Graduates

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans announced the signing of a strategic partnership agreement with Nova Services, a leading provider of contact center services in Jordan. The agreement was signed in the presence of Eng. Mothanna Gharaibeh, representing the Board of Directors, Mr. Isam Bayazidi. Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Nova Services, and Eng. Noor Al Hommoud, Al Aman Fund Director.

The partnership aims to provide specialized employment opportunities for a number of Al Aman graduates in the fields of sales and customer service, supporting their integration into the labor market and empowering them to build stable and sustainable careers.

This partnership reflects Nova Services’ commitment to empowering and supporting orphaned youth by creating meaningful and sustainable employment opportunities that contribute to community development and help prepare a generation capable of playing an active role in advancing the business services sector across the region.

The collaboration also aligns with Al Aman Fund’s long-standing vision, built throughout its twenty-year journey to support its beneficiaries beyond graduation by connecting them with employment opportunities through its wide network of partners across various sectors. These opportunities are carefully matched with graduates’ academic backgrounds and skill sets, helping enhance their prospects for long-term professional growth and success.

During the signing ceremony, Mr. Isam Bayazidi, Chief Executive Officer of Nova Services, stated: “We are delighted to partner with Al Aman Fund. This agreement reflects our commitment to empowering orphaned youth and opening new professional pathways for them. We have great confidence in the capabilities of Al Aman graduates and remain committed to providing them with the support they need to enter the labor market with confidence and pursue careers that align with their skills and aspirations.”

For her part, Eng. Noor Al Hommoud, Al Aman Fund Director, said: “Our partnership with Nova Services reflects a shared commitment to supporting and empowering orphaned youth as they embark on their professional journeys. At Al Aman Fund, our role does not end when beneficiaries complete their education. We remain committed to providing the tools, opportunities, and guidance that help our graduates build successful careers and achieve stability and independence.”

As part of its commitment to enhancing the professional readiness of its beneficiaries, Al Aman Fund continues to implement a series of specialized training programs through its SIDE Program. This curriculum is designed to strengthen beneficiaries’ professional skills and prepare them for the labor market through training in professional CV writing, workplace communication, professional etiquette, and interview preparation. Such efforts provide graduates with a competitive advantage and increase their opportunities for long-term career success.

news.title: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans: The Order of Independence Recognizes Two Decades of Empowering Orphaned Youth Under the Royal Vision
news.excerpt: In a noble Royal gesture that reflects appreciation for national and humanitarian service, His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein bestowed the Order of Al Istiqlal (Independence) of the First Degree upon Al Aman Fun

body.text: In a noble Royal gesture that reflects appreciation for national and humanitarian service, His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein bestowed the Order of Al Istiqlal (Independence) of the First Degree upon Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans. This honor recognizes the Fund’s pioneering and distinguished role in providing a comprehensive support system for orphaned youth, including graduates of care homes and orphaned youth from all governorates of the Kingdom. The honor was conferred on the occasion of Jordan’s 80th Independence Day, and the medal was received by Al Aman Fund Director, Eng. Noor Homoud.

This honor, which is granted to those who have made distinguished contributions to Jordan’s progress and modernization, recognizes the Fund’s exceptional impact and marks the culmination of two decades of empowerment and unwavering commitment. The Fund was established as a Royal initiative by Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah, who has provided the Fund with exceptional patronage since its inception. Driven by her profound dedication to orphaned youth in Jordan, Her Majesty has consistently worked to ensure that every orphaned youth is afforded a fair opportunity in life, firmly believing that investing in their future is an investment in the future of Jordan.

This recognition embodies the profound and sustainable impact that Al Aman Fund has achieved in the lives of its beneficiaries. For two decades, the Fund has gone beyond providing educational and livelihood support; it has successfully built an integrated system that has empowered thousands of orphaned youth to navigate critical life challenges and transition toward self-reliance and independence. The Fund has supported more than 5,050 orphaned youth in completing their educational journeys, including bachelor’s degrees, diplomas, and vocational training programs. Of these, 3,766 have successfully graduated, with 78% entering the labor market, transforming countless challenges into stories of professional and personal success. Today, the Fund’s graduates contribute to society equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to lead dignified and stable lives, reflecting the true impact of investing in people.

Following the ceremony, Eng. Noor Homoud expressed her pride and deep gratitude for this prestigious honor, stating: “We extend our deepest gratitude and highest appreciation to His Majesty King Abdullah II for this recognition, which we cherish as a badge of honor for Al Aman Fund. At this moment, we also express our profound respect for the visionary leadership of Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah since the Fund’s establishment in 2006. Her Majesty has been, and remains, the primary catalyst for this journey, consistently demonstrating her dedication through her continued interest in the development of our youth and her genuine pride in their success stories.”

She added, “We dedicate this achievement to all our partners who believed in our mission, affirming that the synergy of national efforts is the cornerstone of empowering orphaned youth and building a better future for them.”

Al Aman Fund reaffirms its commitment to continuing its noble mission, pledging to further develop and expand its programs to meet the demands of the modern era and the evolving challenges of the labor market. The Fund remains a pioneering institution dedicated to creating opportunities and transforming youth aspirations into tangible realities that contribute to national development.

news.title: Queen Rania Attends Charity Dinner Marking 20th Anniversary of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans
news.excerpt: (Office of Her Majesty – Press Department – Amman) – Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah attended a charity dinner in Amman on Tuesday marking the 20th anniversary of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, reaffirming t

body.text: (Office of Her Majesty – Press Department – Amman) – Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah attended a charity dinner in Amman on Tuesday marking the 20th anniversary of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, reaffirming the non-profit’s two-decade commitment to expanding educational opportunities for vulnerable youth across Jordan.

Held under Her Majesty’s patronage, the event celebrated the achievements of the Fund’s beneficiaries, expressed appreciation for its donors for their sustained support, and aimed to secure funding for a new cohort of Jordanian youth to complete their higher education.

Originally launched by Queen Rania in 2003 as a charitable campaign, Al Aman Fund was officially registered as a non-profit organization in 2006, becoming the first Jordanian institution of its kind dedicated to supporting the underserved demographic of orphans aged 18 and above. Named for the Arabic word for “security,” Al Aman aims to provide orphaned youth with opportunities to obtain higher education, and achieve professional and personal success in adulthood.

Upon Queen Rania’s arrival at the Grand Hyatt Amman hotel, she joined members of Al Aman Fund’s Board of Directors and General Assembly for a brief meeting with a number of its most prominent donors and partners. Her Majesty expressed her appreciation for the organizations and members of the public who support the Fund and help make its humanitarian mission a reality.

The charity event featured testimonials from a number of the Fund’s former beneficiaries, who explained how the organization’s support empowered them to complete their studies and successfully integrate into the workforce and wider society.

The dinner also included remarks from Al Aman’s Director General, Noor Homoud, who expressed her pride in the many young men and women whom Al Aman Fund has helped achieve independence through its financial and non-financial support.

“Today, we are proud to have expanded our services to include orphaned youth across all of Jordan’s governorates, supporting not only those who have graduated from care homes, but also those whose circumstances may have otherwise prevented them from completing their education,” Homoud said.
“In addition to education, housing, livelihood support, and health insurance, the Fund has provided training in 75 social, economic, and digital skills,” she added.

To date, Al Aman Fund has impacted the lives of more than 5,000 young men and women who have received fully-funded scholarships to complete university degrees, attend community college, or receive vocational training.

The charity event was supported by 38 sponsors and partners across the public and private sector. Platinum sponsors included Housing Bank for Trade and Finance, Jordan Bromine Company, Aqaba Development Corporation, and Equiti Group, while Gold sponsors included Arab Potash Company and Al Waha for Cars.

news.title: On Arab Orphans Day, Al Aman Fund Affirms: Empowering Orphaned Youth is a Responsibility, Not Sympathy
news.excerpt: April 2026 – On Arab Orphans Day, observed annually on the first Friday of April, Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans celebrates two decades of sustainable impact. Over the past 20 years, the Fund has empowered thousa

body.text: April 2026 – On Arab Orphans Day, observed annually on the first Friday of April, Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans celebrates two decades of sustainable impact. Over the past 20 years, the Fund has empowered thousands of orphaned youth, graduates of residential care homes, as well as youth across the Kingdom whose economic circumstances have hindered their access to education.

On this occasion, the Fund reaffirms its national mission, calling on individuals and institutions across both the public and private sectors to unite efforts around a two-decade journey of support and empowerment. It emphasizes that investing in the education and empowerment of orphaned youth is not a choice, but a fundamental responsibility shared by all members of society to build a more stable and prosperous future for these young individuals.

Arab Orphans Day serves as an important opportunity to raise societal awareness of the challenges and needs of orphaned youth, reinforcing that supporting them is not limited to a single day each year, but rather a continuous commitment whose impact extends across society as a whole. In this context, Al Aman Fund plays a vital role in transforming awareness into tangible impact through its innovative and diverse programs, which engage various segments of society in supporting education, living expenses, mental health, and capacity-building programs. These efforts enable youth to compete with their peers and successfully transition into independent, self-reliant lives.

Over the past two decades, Al Aman Fund has driven meaningful, lasting change in the lives of thousands of orphaned youth, redefining what long-term empowerment truly means. The Fund provides a comprehensive support system that accompanies youth throughout their educational and life journeys, extending into their integration into the labor market, the establishment of their own businesses and families, and ultimately leading to safe and independent lives. Since its establishment, the Fund has impacted the lives of over 5,000 orphaned youth through fully funded scholarships spanning 4 to 5 years across various academic disciplines, and up to 6 years for medical fields, in addition to vocational training and college programs ranging from one to two years.

This reflects the scale of the shared commitment required from both the Fund and society to enable orphaned youth to build dignified and independent lives. The average annual sponsorship per beneficiary from residential care graduates exceeds approximately JOD 7,000, depending on the field of study and academic pathway, in addition to living costs including housing, stipends, health insurance, and empowerment and capacity-building programs. This figure represents the level of annual investment required to support each beneficiary throughout their journey until they achieve independence and build their future with confidence.

The Fund also emphasizes that the impact achieved over the years would not have been possible without a broad network of partners and supporters. Institutions from both the public and private sectors, as well as schools and educational institutions, have played a key role in supporting the Fund’s programs and expanding its reach to a greater number of beneficiaries. The Fund further invites individuals to contribute to creating lasting impact in the lives of orphaned youth by donating through its website and selecting a support program with ease: https://alamanfund.jo/ar/ways-to-give-ar/donate-ar helping expand its reach and empower even more young people.

news.title: Al Aman Fund Opens Applications for Bachelor’s Degree Scholarships for Orphaned Youth
news.excerpt: Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has announced the opening of applications for bachelor’s degree scholarships for orphaned youth from across Jordan for the 2026-2027 academic year. The announcement reflects the mis

body.text: Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has announced the opening of applications for bachelor’s degree scholarships for orphaned youth from across Jordan for the 2026-2027 academic year. The announcement reflects the mission put forth by Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah, who founded Al-Aman in 2006 to support orphans beyond the age of 18 by providing education and training opportunities to help them build their professional future.

The scholarships, which will cover all registration and tuition fees, are open to orphaned youth currently enrolled in public universities under the competitive admission system. Applicants must be no older than 20, and must have successfully completed at least their first academic semester with a minimum grade of “Good.”

Eligible students can submit their applications and review the full eligibility requirements through the application portal, eligibility.alamanfund.jo, by March 19, 2026. A link to the portal has also been shared on Al-Aman’s official social media platforms, on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.

All applications undergo a clear and transparent evaluation process. After applicants submit the required certified documents, applications are carefully reviewed according to approved criteria and evaluation standards. This process ensures that the most eligible and deserving students are selected, while maintaining fairness and equal opportunity for all applicants.

Over the past 20 years, Al-Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has assisted thousands of orphaned youth through educational, skill development, and psychosocial support programs across all Jordanian governorates. This support has helped beneficiaries complete their education, access the job market, and build dignified and independent lives. Through its education scholarships, the Fund has helped thousands of orphaned youth, graduate and embark on their professional careers. Now marking its 20th year, Al-Aman Fund continues to expand its programs, reaffirming its commitment to creating greater opportunities for orphaned youth across Jordan.

news.title: Al Aman Fund Celebrates Two Decades of Impact with the Launch of Its 2026 Ramadan Campaign
news.excerpt: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has launched its 2026 Ramadan campaign, coinciding with the Fund’s 20th anniversary since its establishment in 2006. The campaign calls on individuals to direct their Zakat and char

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has launched its 2026 Ramadan campaign, coinciding with the Fund’s 20th anniversary since its establishment in 2006. The campaign calls on individuals to direct their Zakat and charitable giving during the holy month toward supporting the orphaned youth and enabling them to continue their education and build independent futures.

Al Aman Fund had earlier paved the way for the launch of this year’s campaign through a teaser campaign that preceded the official announcement, drawing attention to the reality that turning 18 does not carry the same meaning for every youth. The teaser sparked widespread public curiosity about the nature of the campaign and the sensitive issue it aimed to highlight, focusing on the challenges faced by orphaned youth upon leaving the care homes at the age of 18. While many of their peers celebrate this milestone as the beginning of independence supported by their families, however, for an orphaned youth it can instead mark the start of uncertainty and early responsibility in the absence of immediate family support.

This interactive approach generated significant engagement and helped set the stage for the campaign’s central message, emphasizing the essential role of Al Aman Fund in providing comprehensive support and stability for orphaned youth, enabling them to move toward a future built on dignity and independence.

The campaign video portrays the pivotal moment an orphaned youth experiences upon leaving care home and entering a more sensitive stage of life without the direct family support. It then documents how the journey transforms through the Fund’s support, which provides educational and livelihood support, along with capacity building programs that enable beneficiaries to continue their path with confidence and independence.

The video concludes with a reflective moment as the orphaned youth looks back on the path he has taken since leaving the care home at the age of 18. Twenty years later, his journey mirrors the two decades since the establishment of Al Aman Fund, bringing the story full circle. The scene captures the legacy of “Two Decades of Al Aman,” revealing how consistent support can transform uncertainty into opportunity. Some of Al Aman’s beneficiaries also appear in the video, proudly sharing their experiences and expressing their pride in being part of Al Aman’s journey, which has supported them in continuing their education and building independent futures.

Al Aman Fund confirmed holding an official Fatwa from the Jordanian Iftaa Department (Fatwa No. 7/2010), which permits the use of Zakat funds to support orphaned youth over the age of 18 who do not have financial means. Zakat contributions and donations are directed toward covering university, college, and vocational training tuition fees, in addition to monthly allowance, housing, health insurance, and psychosocial and capacity building programs.
In addition, Zakat Al-Fitr will be distributed as Eidiyeh to beneficiaries on the first day of Eid Al-Fitr, ensuring that orphaned youth can celebrate the holiday with dignity and joy.

To ensure donors can easily contribute their Zakat and charitable donations during Ramadan, the Fund will be present through donation booths at several locations including City Mall (P1 level), Miles Supermarket at Mecca Mall, Cozmo, and Abdali Mall (GF). The campaign also includes community partnerships that facilitate donations and expand outreach through checkout campaigns at all Sameh Mall and Food Gate Market branches.

Al Aman Fund also provides multiple convenient and secure donation channels for individuals, including direct calls via 065664427, CliQ under the name Amanfund, eFAWATEERcom, all banking applications under the charities list, as well as delivery applications such as Talabat and Careem.

news.title: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans Wins Second Place at Al Hussein bin Abdullah II Award for Voluntary Service
news.excerpt: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has won second place at Al Hussein bin Abdullah II Award for Voluntary Service under the category of “Best Volunteer Project by a Non-Profit Organization” The Fund’s Director Eng. N

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has won second place at Al Hussein bin Abdullah II Award for Voluntary Service under the category of “Best Volunteer Project by a Non-Profit Organization” The Fund’s Director Eng. Noor Al Hommoud, had the honor of receiving the award during the ceremony announcing the winners, held under the patronage of His Royal Highness Crown Prince Al Hussein bin Abdullah II. The Fund received this award for its “Empty Chair” program, an innovative model that engages school and university students in supporting the education of orphaned youth benefiting from the Fund. The program empowers students to create inspiring volunteer-led initiatives aimed at raising funds to cover university education costs for Al Aman youth. Al Aman Fund qualified for the award after a strong competition that included several non-profit organizations. The “Empty Chair” program was recognized for successfully transforming student volunteering in schools and universities into a space for innovation and social responsibility, where volunteers design initiatives that directly contribute to securing education costs for Al Aman youth and enabling them to pursue their dreams, just as the volunteers themselves benefit from educational opportunities that shape their own futures. It is worth noting that the “Empty Chair” program began as an initiative exploring how and why school students can be engaged in Al Aman Fund’s volunteer work. What started with an empty seat evolved into a real educational opportunity. The program was developed in line with the Fund’s mission to transform support for orphaned youth into a shared community responsibility that brings together people of all ages. The program engages students in grades 11 and 12 in designing various volunteer initiatives that aim to raise funds to cover the educational costs of one of the Fund’s beneficiaries. To enhance transparency, each student group is provided with a dedicated online page that shows the progress of donations and their direct impact on the sponsored student, creating a clear connection between donors and beneficiaries. The program’s win serves as a mark of trust and credibility, affirming the effectiveness of this innovative volunteer model, as well as its transparency in tracking impact and delivering support to those who need it. The program is also distinguished by its sustainability and ability to evolve, as the experience is passed on from one class to another within the same school, allowing its impact to grow year after year and become a culture of collective action among students. Each time, the “Empty Chair” becomes a symbol of a university seat filled by one of Al Aman’s beneficiaries, while the volunteers become part of a story of change that begins with awareness and ends with an opportunity created through their own initiatives. The program has succeeded in creating an environment where students learn the values of giving, teamwork, and leadership, while deepening their understanding of the educational and living needs of orphaned youth. Since its launch, the program has engaged 140 volunteers from 9 schools, supporting the education of 11 orphaned youth benefiting from Al Aman Fund, creating a real impact that continues to expand year after year. Eng. Noor Al Hommoud affirmed that this achievement is proof that the Fund’s vision to expand its impact is being translated into action through volunteer programs such as the “Empty Chair.” She added that the Fund will continue developing programs that empower youth and open doors to a more confident future. This recognition marks a new milestone in Al Aman Fund’s nearly twenty-year journey of empowering orphaned youth and promoting a culture of giving and social responsibility through volunteer programs that create tangible impact in the future of Al Aman youth.

body.text: Al Aqaba Development Corporation has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, aimed at empowering orphaned youth in Aqaba through the “Vocational Training Scholarship for Orphaned Youth in Aqaba” program. The initiative seeks to provide specialized vocational training opportunities tailored to the needs of the local labor market, helping orphaned youth enhance their employability and achieve self-reliance..

Under this agreement, Al Aqaba Development Corporation will provide financial support covering 28 orphaned youth (both male and female) from Aqaba. The funds will be directed toward the Fund’s educational and training programs implemented in the governorate, as part of the Corporation’s corporate social responsibility (CSR) vision focused on empowering local communities and fostering integrated human development.
For the first time in Aqaba, these training grants will be announced and opened for applications on a competitive and transparent basis, with full details of the scholarships to be revealed soon.

This collaboration builds upon Al Aqaba Development Corporation’s ongoing efforts to support national initiatives aimed at building youth capacities and expanding opportunities for orphaned graduates from care centers, in alignment with Aqaba’s sustainable development approach — one that integrates economic and social growth within the framework of the Aqaba Special Economic Zone’s mission.

Hussein Al-Safadi, CEO of Al Aqaba Development Corporation, emphasized the importance of investing in people, stating: “True development is not measured by the scale of projects alone, but by our ability to empower people and create opportunities for them. This agreement with Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans reflects our practical commitment to supporting a deserving group of young Jordanians who should find in Aqaba an environment that embraces them and equips them with the tools for a better future.”

Al-Safadi also affirmed that the Corporation will continue to support vocational training and applied education programs for orphaned youth, ensuring they acquire the practical skills required by the professional sectors operating within the Special Economic Zone.

Noor Homoud, General Manager of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, expressed her appreciation to Al Aqaba Development Corporation for its initiative to support the Fund’s efforts in Aqaba, noting that this partnership represents a model for empowering orphaned youth through education and vocational training. and she said: “The support provided by Al Aqaba Development Corporation will help us expand our programs in southern Jordan, particularly in Aqaba, offering real opportunities for orphaned youth to gain skills and confidently enter the labor market. Since its establishment, Al Aman Fund has been dedicated to building secure and sustainable futures for orphaned youth above the age of 18 through comprehensive programs that include university, diploma, and vocational education, as well as living support. Collaborations with leading national institutions such as Al Aqaba Development Corporation strengthen our shared mission to empower less fortunate youth to live with dignity and independence.”

news.title: Queen Rania Meets Small Business Owners and Al Aman Fund Beneficiaries in Ma’an
news.excerpt: (Office of Her Majesty – Press Department – Ma’an) – Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah visited Ma’an Governorate on Wednesday, where she met with a number of small business owners who have benefited from economic empow

body.text: (Office of Her Majesty – Press Department – Ma’an) – Her Majesty Queen Rania Al Abdullah visited Ma’an Governorate on Wednesday, where she met with a number of small business owners who have benefited from economic empowerment programs supported by the Royal Hashemite Court (RHC), as well as beneficiaries supported by Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans.

Queen Rania began her visit to Ma’an at a home-based children’s photography studio, established by married couple Yasser Abu Omar and Widd al Ruwad after receiving a grant from the RHC. The couple showed Her Majesty around their studio, which now serves as their family’s primary source of income.
The Queen also met with beneficiaries of an RHC grant scheme, as well as leaders of a number of local associations, at the Founding King’s Residence.

At the meeting, attended by Ma’an Governor Khaled Hajjaj, President of the Community Centers Associations (CCA) Dr. Firyal Saleh, and Jordan Heritage Revival Company CEO Muayyad Abu Rumman, Dr. Saleh presented the methodology and impact of the grant scheme.

Initiated by the RHC and implemented by the CCA in coordination with 11 local societies, the scheme has disbursed grants to 124 families in the governorate, resulting in the expansion of 88 income-generating projects.
Her Majesty also heard from grant beneficiaries, who explained how financial support has helped them establish their own projects and strengthen their economic independence.

During the meeting, Queen Rania noted the diversity of the presented income-generating projects, and commended the small business owners and social initiatives for their collaborative spirit. She also highlighted the vital role that Ma’an’s women play in its various sectors.
Queen Rania also sat down with a group of Ma’an-based beneficiaries of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, as well as the fund’s general manager, Nour Homoud.

Launched by Her Majesty in 2006, Al Aman aims to provide orphans above the age of 18 with opportunities to obtain higher education and vocational training. Homoud explained that the fund collaborates with four civil societies in Ma’an, supporting a total of 279 students in the governorate to date, 196 of whom have completed their studies.
While in Ma’an, the Queen stopped by a sweet kiosk run by local youth, Mohammad Ma’ani. The kiosk is known in the area for its ‘harissa Ma’aniya’, a popular local semolina-based dessert.

news.title: Al Aman Fund Concludes the “Innovation and Digital Empowerment Journey” Trainings for Orphaned Youth Supported by Bromine Jordan
news.excerpt: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans held a closing ceremony for its “Innovation and Digital Empowerment Journey” training program, conducted during the first three weeks of September with the support of the Fund’s Dia

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans held a closing ceremony for its “Innovation and Digital Empowerment Journey” training program, conducted during the first three weeks of September with the support of the Fund’s Diamond Partner, Bromine Jordan. The event brought together 43 orphaned youth beneficiaries from Aqaba and Karak, alongside representatives and team members from both organizations.

The ceremony marked the culmination of three weeks of intensive training in digital skills, artificial intelligence, and entrepreneurship. Participants explored topics such as the basics of AI, the use of modern digital tools, and engaged in interactive sessions and brainstorming workshops that helped them develop innovative ideas and early-stage entrepreneurial projects.

Over the past two years, Bromine Jordan has provided strategic Diamond-level support to Al Aman Fund’s programs, covering educational scholarships and living expenses for orphaned youth. Through this partnership, 45 beneficiaries have received support, including two who graduated last year thanks to the scholarship. Currently, 43 beneficiaries benefit from coverage of their university, diploma, and vocational training costs. The partnership also includes housing support for six youth, monthly stipends for nine others, and empowerment programs that benefit all participants. This sustained commitment reflects Bromine Jordan’s dedication to corporate social responsibility and its investment in education and youth empowerment for a brighter future.
Noor Homoud, General Manager of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, highlighted the importance of the partnership, stating:

“Our collaboration with Bromine Jordan represents an inspiring model of sustainable corporate social responsibility. We are proud of this partnership with a company that truly believes in our mission. Through their ongoing support, we’ve been able to open new doors for our youth, equipping them with the skills they need to face life’s challenges and become self-reliant leaders of tomorrow. Bromine is one of our key and most dedicated partners, leaving a lasting impact on our beneficiaries’ lives and empowering their journey toward a brighter future.”

In his welcoming remarks, Tariq Al-Kharabsheh, Programs Manager at Al Aman Fund, expressed his pride in the achievements of the youth and the positive outcomes of the training series. He reaffirmed the Fund’s commitment to developing youth skills across diverse fields, especially in emerging technologies and artificial intelligence, to enhance their readiness for the labor market.

The event also featured a video presentation capturing the highlights of the “Innovation and Digital Empowerment Journey”, showcasing the experiences and progress of the 43 participants who successfully completed the program. The ceremony concluded with a certificate distribution and recognition segment, celebrating the achievements of the youth in an atmosphere of pride and gratitude for the profound impact this partnership continues to create in their lives.

news.title: Partnership renewal between Al Aman fund for the Future of Orphans and Jerusalem Insurance Company

body.text: Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans has announced the renewal of its partnership with Jerusalem Insurance Company. Over the past three years, Jerusalem Insurance Company has supported the students of Al Aman Fund, emphasizing the importance of supporting orphaned youth in Jordan and providing them with equal opportunities as their peers in society. Commenting on this partnership, Mr. Imad Morrar, CEO of Jerusalem Insurance Company, stated: “Our vision at Jerusalem Insurance extends beyond merely providing insurance services to individuals and companies. It encompasses our social responsibility towards the less fortunate and serving humanitarian causes as much as possible. We are proud to collaborate with Al Aman Fund and support its mission to empower orphaned youth in the community and invest in their future.”

Ms. Noor Al Homoud, the General Manager of Al Aman Fund for the Future of Orphans, said: “This ongoing cooperation between the fund and Jerusalem Insurance Company reflects a shared commitment to supporting orphaned youth and education as part of the company’s corporate social responsibility strategy.” She further emphasized, “The primary goals of Al Aman Fund are to create a bright future for orphaned youth, which can only be achieved through strategic cooperation and partnerships with institutions that believe in our orphaned youth and the importance of supporting them and providing them with equal opportunities.”
It is worth mentioning that Jerusalem Insurance Company is a leading insurance provider in Jordan, offering innovative insurance solutions for businesses, families, and individuals across Jordan.
